title: Article 122 — Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament

content.overview: Article 122 provides that the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure, and that no officer or member of Parliament in whom powers are vested by or under the Constitution for regulating procedure or the conduct of business or for maintaining order in Parliament shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise by him of those powers.
content.glance: Courts cannot question validity of parliamentary proceedings for mere irregularity of procedure. Officers/members regulating procedure/order not subject to court jurisdiction for exercise of those powers.
content.study:
Article 122 protects internal parliamentary proceedings from judicial scrutiny on grounds of procedural irregularity, and protects officers and members exercising constitutional powers of procedure and order from court jurisdiction in respect of that exercise.

Scope is not unlimited: the provision targets irregularity of procedure and the listed regulatory powers; it does not oust all judicial review of constitutional limits (e.g. where a claim is that Parliament has acted outside its constitutional power altogether). Examination should state the text accurately and note the distinction between procedural irregularity and substantive constitutional limits.

Examination: no inquiry into validity for irregularity of procedure; protection of officers/members on procedure/order powers; distinguish from substantive constitutional challenges.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Validity of parliamentary proceedings not to be called in question on the ground of alleged irregularity of procedure.
2. Officers/members vested with powers to regulate procedure, conduct of business, or maintain order are not subject to court jurisdiction in respect of the exercise of those powers.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 122 provide regarding courts and parliamentary proceedings?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 122 provides that the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure. No officer or member of Parliament in whom powers are vested by or under the Constitution for regulating procedure or the conduct of business or for maintaining order in Parliament shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise by him of those powers.

examTips: No court inquiry into validity for procedural irregularity; officers protected on procedure/order powers.

keyTakeaways: Art 122: courts not to inquire into parliamentary proceedings for procedural irregularity.
